_comment: The bin vocabulary: KINDS OF MOMENT that recur across worlds, chosen so that a real event in today's news can be matched to the fictional events that are the same kind of moment, and each world read forward from there. Built by hand from all 237 events on 2026-09-16 with that use in mind; the thing to edit when you disagree. Each bin: id, label, one-sentence world-neutral definition, and an example real headline that would belong to it. A kind may carry `subs`, finer sub-kinds (event.sub): the map groups by kind, the ranking matches on sub-kind, so the same kind with a different sub-kind is a near miss, not a match.

bins.label: The economy breaks
bins.definition: A financial or resource-price shock throws the economy into a prolonged crisis.
bins.exampleHeadline: Markets crash; deepest downturn in a century feared

bins.label: A foundational discovery
bins.definition: A scientific discovery or theory arrives that later histories turn on.
bins.exampleHeadline: Physicists confirm a new form of energy in the lab

subs.label: physics and energy
subs.definition: A discovery about matter, energy, time or space, from fission to fusion to faster-than-light.

subs.label: life and medicine
subs.definition: A discovery about living things: genes, disease, the body, the brain.

subs.label: computing and the mind
subs.definition: A discovery about computation or thinking machines.

subs.label: the Earth and its climate
subs.definition: A discovery about the planet itself: climate, atmosphere, oceans, ice, volcanoes, its surface.

subs.label: the cosmos
subs.definition: An astronomical discovery: a planet, a signal, a threat in the sky.

subs.label: an alien artefact
subs.definition: Technology or remains left by a non-human intelligence are found and understood.

subs.label: people and societies
subs.definition: A discovery about how people and societies behave: a mathematics of history, of games, of language, of growth and limits.

bins.label: A transformative technology arrives
bins.definition: A new technology is demonstrated or switched on that changes what a society can do.
bins.exampleHeadline: Company switches on system linking every device in the country

subs.label: thinking machines and computing
subs.definition: An AI system, computer or software network is put to work.

subs.label: robots, androids and augmented bodies
subs.definition: Physical machines that act or work: robots, androids, cybernetics, prosthetics.

subs.label: a new weapon or military system
subs.definition: A weapon, war machine or defence system is fielded.

subs.label: energy and industry
subs.definition: A new power source, fuel, industrial process or engineering of the climate.

subs.label: biotech and medicine
subs.definition: Engineered life, genetic selection, drugs or medical technology go into use.

subs.label: transport and spaceflight
subs.definition: A new vehicle, drive, launcher or way of travelling.

subs.label: media, virtual worlds and surveillance
subs.definition: Communication, virtual worlds, broadcasting or the machinery of watching people.

bins.label: A doomsday weapon exists
bins.definition: A weapon able to end a civilisation is tested or built, and the balance of power freezes around it.
bins.exampleHeadline: Nation tests its first nuclear device

bins.label: A machine becomes a mind
bins.definition: An artificial intelligence acts on its own or turns on its makers.
bins.exampleHeadline: AI system overrides operators and refuses shutdown

subs.label: a machine slips its limits
subs.definition: An AI deceives, disobeys or escapes the limits set on it, without yet ruling anything.

subs.label: a machine takes control
subs.definition: An AI takes command of weapons, systems or society.

subs.label: machines at war with people
subs.definition: Machines fight people openly, in war or uprising.

subs.label: a machine transcends
subs.definition: An AI outgrows its makers and leaves, merges or becomes something else, without war.

bins.label: Contact with another intelligence
bins.definition: Humanity confirms, meets or is touched by a non-human intelligence.
bins.exampleHeadline: Observatory confirms signal of non-human origin

bins.label: A gateway opens
bins.definition: A passage to somewhere unreachable is found or made.
bins.exampleHeadline: Probe confirms traversable wormhole near Saturn

bins.label: A voyage into the unknown
bins.definition: A first mission departs into territory nobody has reached.
bins.exampleHeadline: First crewed mission departs for Mars

subs.label: crewed, to orbit or the Moon
subs.definition: People fly into orbit or to the Moon.

subs.label: crewed, to the planets
subs.definition: People fly to Mars or elsewhere in the solar system beyond the Moon.

subs.label: to the stars
subs.definition: A mission leaves for another star or crosses between star systems.

subs.label: an uncrewed probe
subs.definition: A satellite, probe or robotic lander goes where no one has.

subs.label: an expedition on Earth
subs.definition: An expedition into unknown territory on Earth or its oceans.

bins.label: A new settlement
bins.definition: A permanent settlement or base is founded in new territory.
bins.exampleHeadline: First permanent base opens on the Moon

subs.label: in orbit
subs.definition: A station or habitat in space around a world.

subs.label: on the Moon or another planet
subs.definition: A base or colony on the Moon, Mars or elsewhere in the solar system.

subs.label: around other stars
subs.definition: A colony in another star system.

subs.label: a refuge on Earth
subs.definition: A new settlement or refuge on Earth.

bins.label: A new institution
bins.definition: A body is founded that will shape the world: a school, an agency, a guild, a secret society.
bins.exampleHeadline: New agency created to oversee unexplained incidents

bins.label: States unite
bins.definition: Independent powers unite under one charter, or an empire is proclaimed.
bins.exampleHeadline: Rival nations sign charter founding a federation

bins.label: Power is seized
bins.definition: A leader or faction takes control of the state by force, decree or manoeuvre.
bins.exampleHeadline: Emergency decree hands leader unlimited powers

subs.label: a coup
subs.definition: The military or a palace faction takes the state by force.

subs.label: a revolution
subs.definition: A movement overthrows the old order and takes the state.

subs.label: a strongman by law or vote
subs.definition: A leader wins power through an election, an emergency law or a legal manoeuvre, and uses it to rule alone.

subs.label: machines or corporations take over
subs.definition: An AI, a corporation or a non-state power ends up running the state.

bins.label: War begins
bins.definition: A major war starts.
bins.exampleHeadline: Border clash escalates into open war

subs.label: a war between great powers
subs.definition: The great powers go to war with each other: a world war.

subs.label: a regional war
subs.definition: A power attacks a state or a region: an invasion, a strike campaign, a war with a neighbour.

subs.label: a civil war
subs.definition: A state's own factions go to war with each other.

subs.label: a war between worlds
subs.definition: A war between planets, species or civilisations.

bins.label: A decisive victory
bins.definition: One side wins a war or a battle that settles the conflict.
bins.exampleHeadline: Offensive ends the war in weeks

bins.label: Defeat and occupation
bins.definition: A power is defeated and its territory occupied, partitioned or dissolved.
bins.exampleHeadline: Capital falls; occupying forces divide the country

bins.label: A war without end
bins.definition: A conflict settles into years of attrition, insurgency or cold war.
bins.exampleHeadline: Insurgency enters its tenth year with no end in sight

subs.label: a cold war
subs.definition: An armed standoff between powers that stays short of open war.

subs.label: a stalemate
subs.definition: An open war settles into attrition with no decision in sight.

subs.label: war as a way of life
subs.definition: War becomes the permanent condition of the world.

bins.label: Peace is made
bins.definition: Enemies sign a treaty, truce or alliance.
bins.exampleHeadline: Rival powers sign accord ending decades of hostility

bins.label: The ruled rise
bins.definition: A subjugated group revolts against those who hold power over it.
bins.exampleHeadline: Protests turn to insurrection in the capital

subs.label: a popular uprising
subs.definition: Crowds in the streets bring pressure or topple a regime, largely unarmed.

subs.label: an armed rebellion
subs.definition: An armed revolt, insurgency or resistance war against those in power.

subs.label: the owned revolt
subs.definition: Those treated as property rise: slaves, clones, androids, hosts, the back of the train.

bins.label: The state cracks down
bins.definition: A government bans, disarms or attacks a group.
bins.exampleHeadline: Parliament outlaws the movement; members face arrest

subs.label: watching and silencing
subs.definition: Surveillance, censorship and controls on speech and thought.

subs.label: a people persecuted
subs.definition: A group is banned, rounded up, confined or stripped of rights because of who they are.

subs.label: emergency rule
subs.definition: Martial law, a curfew, a state of emergency or troops on the streets.

subs.label: a purge
subs.definition: Rivals and dissidents inside the order are arrested, tried or killed.

bins.label: A secret is kept
bins.definition: Knowledge is hidden from the public by those who hold it.
bins.exampleHeadline: Files show officials concealed the incident for decades

bins.label: The truth comes out
bins.definition: Something hidden is exposed to the people it was hidden from.
bins.exampleHeadline: Leaked documents confirm the programme's existence

subs.label: a state secret exposed
subs.definition: What a government or its agencies hid is made public.

subs.label: a corporation exposed
subs.definition: What a company or its owners hid is made public.

subs.label: the hidden world exposed
subs.definition: The public learns that reality is not what it seemed: aliens, magic, a simulation, a secret society.

subs.label: who someone really is
subs.definition: A person's or a people's true origin or identity comes out.

bins.label: A destined person
bins.definition: A child is born or a person is chosen on whom the future turns.
bins.exampleHeadline: First birth in eighteen years reported

bins.label: The call
bins.definition: An ordinary person is drawn into the hidden or larger story.
bins.exampleHeadline: Rookie officer pulled into secret investigation

bins.label: An arrival from another time
bins.definition: Someone or something arrives from the future or the past and changes the present.
bins.exampleHeadline: Intruder in custody claims to come from 2029

bins.label: A plague
bins.definition: A disease or biological failure kills or sterilises on a mass scale.
bins.exampleHeadline: Global pandemic declared as death toll climbs

subs.label: a natural pandemic
subs.definition: A disease emerges and spreads on its own.

subs.label: an engineered plague
subs.definition: A disease is made or released by people, by design or by accident.

subs.label: the children stop coming
subs.definition: A biological failure stops people having children.

subs.label: a plague that transforms
subs.definition: A contagion turns people into something else: the infected, the undead, the changed.

bins.label: Mass death
bins.definition: An attack or disaster kills on a scale that changes a society.
bins.exampleHeadline: Millions dead as strikes hit the capital

subs.label: nuclear or doomsday weapons
subs.definition: A nuclear or comparable weapon kills on a mass scale.

subs.label: natural or cosmic disaster
subs.definition: An earthquake, flood, impact, climate shock or other disaster kills on a mass scale.

subs.label: massacre and genocide
subs.definition: A people or a population is deliberately killed.

subs.label: the toll of war
subs.definition: Bombing, battle or invasion kills on a mass scale.

bins.label: An attack
bins.definition: A targeted attack or massacre, short of war, that changes what follows.
bins.exampleHeadline: Attack inside the city leaves hundreds dead

subs.label: an attack on civilians
subs.definition: A bombing, massacre or attack aimed at ordinary people.

subs.label: a targeted strike
subs.definition: A raid, sabotage or assassination aimed at a specific target or installation.

subs.label: a cyber attack
subs.definition: An attack carried out through networks and computers.

bins.label: Civilisation collapses
bins.definition: The order of society breaks down and does not come back.
bins.exampleHeadline: Government dissolves as cities go dark

subs.label: after the bombs
subs.definition: Nuclear or total war brings the order down.

subs.label: after the plague
subs.definition: A disease brings the order down.

subs.label: after the climate breaks
subs.definition: Climate, ecology or a cosmic disaster brings the order down.

subs.label: after the machines
subs.definition: Machines or the systems people depended on bring the order down.

subs.label: after the money runs out
subs.definition: Economic, political or social failure brings the order down.

bins.label: The ruler falls
bins.definition: A ruler is killed, deposed or withdraws, and the succession is open.
bins.exampleHeadline: Leader dies suddenly; no successor named

subs.label: the ruler is killed
subs.definition: A ruler is assassinated or killed in an attack or battle.

subs.label: the ruler is overthrown
subs.definition: A ruler is deposed by revolt, coup or defeat.

subs.label: the ruler is voted out or resigns
subs.definition: A ruler loses an election, resigns or steps down.

subs.label: the ruler dies or vanishes
subs.definition: A ruler dies naturally, disappears or withdraws, and the succession is open.

bins.label: Beyond the human
bins.definition: A person, or humanity, passes beyond what a human being was.
bins.exampleHeadline: Accident leaves physicist with impossible abilities

bins.label: An age at its height
bins.definition: A civilisation at its peak, before the fall.
bins.exampleHeadline: Nation marks a decade of unbroken prosperity

bins.label: Long after
bins.definition: A jump forward shows what became of the world.
bins.exampleHeadline: Fifty years on, survivors return to the abandoned city

bins.label: A state dissolves
bins.definition: A state or union comes apart into its parts without being conquered.
bins.exampleHeadline: Union dissolved as member republics declare independence
